page: UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-3xL4 is a GPU-accelerated virtual server configured on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 CPU architecture with 20 shared vCPUs and 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 12.8 GB per core. The server does not include local storage, meaning external storage volumes must be attached for data persistence. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

The primary hardware feature of this instance is its graphics acceleration subsystem, which consists of three NVIDIA L4 GPUs from the Ada Lovelace architecture family. These GPUs provide a combined total of 72 GB of VRAM. This hardware configuration is designed to support parallel processing tasks that benefit from GPU acceleration, such as machine learning inference, video transcoding, and graphics rendering.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a high density of GPU resources and system memory relative to the shared vCPU allocation. This resource profile makes it suitable for workloads that require substantial GPU memory and system RAM but do not demand fully dedicated, high-performance CPU cores. Appropriate workloads include medium-scale AI inference, data science pipelines, and distributed rendering tasks.
